page: Microsoft Azure E8as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at an operational frequency of 3.525 GHz. It includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB, yielding a high 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration does not include discrete GPU accelerators or bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core processing capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25 percent. In contrast, multi-core metrics, PassMark CPU ratings, and Geekbench scores reside in the middle tier. Small-block cached memory reads achieve 514.78 GB/sec, supporting throughput-heavy cached tasks. However, large-block uncached memory read bandwidth (34.57 GB/sec) and write bandwidth (22.14 GB/sec) fall within the lower 25 percent tier, as does multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 34.61 GB/sec. Operational benchmarks confirm steady intermediate throughput, measuring 8.09 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.5 GB/sec for static web delivery.

The 1:8 core-to-memory allocation provides strong resource density for RAM-bound deployments that do not require proportional multi-threaded compute. Architectural tradeoffs include the lack of AVX-512 instruction support and the absence of ephemeral local disks, which shifts I/O dependency entirely to attached storage. The server profile aligns with memory-heavy enterprise software, including Redis and Memcached caching tiers, medium-scale relational databases, and data transformation jobs that fit primarily within system memory.
description: Microsoft Azure E8as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz across 8 vCPUs (4 physical cores with 2 threads per core) and 64 GB of system memory. This configuration provides a high memory-to-compute ratio of 8 GB per vCPU, suiting memory-intensive workloads. The server features dedicated CPU allocation with 32 MB of L3 cache, hardware AES and SHA cryptographic acceleration, and AVX vector support, though it lacks AVX-512 extensions. In benchmark evaluations, the E8as_v5 exhibits strong single-core CPU throughput, while multi-core processing, static web serving at 9.5 GB/s, and Redis operations at 8.09 million operations per second perform at median levels. Large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidth fall into lower performance tiers. Local disk storage is not bundled, requiring external storage attachments. The instance is designed for in-memory databases, Redis caches, data processing pipelines, and memory-constrained enterprise applications.
